split_question: Should schools teach money skills like inflation, savings and mortgages, even if it means less time on other maths?
angles: yes, put money skills in maths and cut the least useful content, with teachers and parents helping choose what goes
no, keep the maths as it is and teach money skills in separate lessons that do not take maths time
yes, but only after small trials in some schools show pupils keep their maths and learn the money skills
facts_for_writers: The announcement says maths will remove unnecessary content and that GCSE maths will be rebalanced, particularly at foundation tier, towards financial maths and statistics; it does not say what will be cut. [s1]
The announcement gives no start date for the new curriculum and does not mention a public consultation; it says further details will come "in the coming weeks". [s1]

Secondary pupils will be taught what the department calls the "big three" ideas: inflation, compound interest and diversification of risk, which it says are based on research from the Initiative for Financial Decision-Making at Stanford. [s1]

The announcement says 48% of parents believe too little time is spent teaching financial management and that only a third of children recall learning about money at school and finding it useful; it does not name the surveys in the text read. [s1]
In an Opinium poll for Yorkshire Building Society (March 2025), 89% of 2,000 parents of children aged 5 to 17 said financial education should be taught in schools. [s2]
notes: No UK poll was found on money lessons against other maths, so real_share is unset. The Opinium page does not give question wording. A YouGov poll (54% of parents want more school time on personal finance; 55% would cut other curriculum time) was found only in secondary coverage and dates from 2018, so it is not used. The announcement was read in full on GOV.UK; the BBC and other coverage were not opened. The 48% and one-third figures are quoted from the department's own release, whose underlying surveys are not named there.
